steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the React library and useState hook available for use in your component.
successCriteria: The import statement correctly imports React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import syntax. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to import both React and useState from the 'react' package using the correct import syntax.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named EventTypingDemo that returns null for now. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Define a component that matches the name exactly: EventTypingDemo. For now, just make it return null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the EventTypingDemo component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named EventTypingDemo is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: Component is a valid TypeScript functional component
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the EventTypingDemo component. This gives us a starting point to build our event typing demonstration.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there might be a small issue. Make sure your component is named exactly 'EventTypingDemo' and returns null. Check your syntax - you can use either function declaration or arrow function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't seem to be defined correctly. Remember to create a functional component named EventTypingDemo that returns null. In TypeScript, you can use either: 'function EventTypingDemo(): JSX.Element { return null; }' or 'const EventTypingDemo = (): JSX.Element => null;'

steps.title: Initialize text input state
steps.instruction: Inside your EventTypingDemo component, initialize a state variable named 'text' using useState. Set its initial value to an empty string and make sure it's typed as a string.
steps.hint: Use useState<string>('') or let TypeScript infer the type from the initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing string state
const [input, setInput] = useState<string>('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a state variable 'text' initialized to an empty string, ready to store user input.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the text state with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with an empty string initial value and have both the state variable and setter.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to initialize a state variable named 'text' with an empty string value inside your component.

steps.title: Initialize checkbox state
steps.instruction: Inside your EventTypingDemo component, initialize a boolean state variable named 'isChecked' using useState. Set its initial value to false.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with TypeScript generics to specify the type as boolean. The syntax is: useState<boolean>(initialValue).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing boolean state
const [isActive, setIsActive] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a state variable named 'isChecked' with an initial value of false, ready to track checkbox state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized a boolean state variable for tracking checkbox state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with TypeScript generics (<boolean>) and setting the initial value to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a state variable named 'isChecked' with an initial value of false using useState<boolean>(false).

steps.title: Define handleInputChange function
steps.instruction: Inside your EventTypingDemo component, define a function named handleInputChange that takes a parameter typed as React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> and updates the 'text' state with event.target.value.
steps.hint: The function should call setText with the value from the event. Remember to type the parameter properly.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a properly typed handleInputChange function that updates the text state when called with an input change event.
successCriteria: The function must be named handleInputChange, accept a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter, and call setText with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly defined a typed change handler function that will update the text state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named handleInputChange, takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter, and calls setText with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. It should be named handleInputChange, accept a typed event parameter, and update the text state.

steps.title: Define handleCheckboxChange function
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleCheckboxChange that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and updates the 'isChecked' state with event.target.checked. Place it after the existing handleInputChange function.
steps.hint: Create an arrow function with one parameter typed as React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>. Inside the function, call setChecked with event.target.checked.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleCheckboxChange function is defined with proper TypeScript typing for checkbox change events.
successCriteria: The function should be named handleCheckboxChange, accept a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter, and call setChecked with event.target.checked.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed event handler for checkbox changes. The React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> type ensures TypeScript knows event.target.checked exists.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that your function: 1) Has the correct name handleCheckboxChange, 2) Accepts a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter, and 3) Calls setChecked(event.target.checked).
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleCheckboxChange function isn't defined correctly. It should be an arrow function that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> and updates the state with event.target.checked.

steps.title: Define handleButtonClick function
steps.instruction: Define a new function named handleButtonClick inside your EventTypingDemo component. The function should take a React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement> parameter and log a message to the console (e.g., 'Button clicked!').
steps.hint: Add the function after your existing handleCheckboxChange function. Use the React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement> type for the event parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new function handleButtonClick is defined with proper TypeScript typing for button click events.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a typed button click handler. The React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement> type ensures TypeScript knows this event comes from a button element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function has the correct name (handleButtonClick), takes a React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement> parameter, and logs a message to the console.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleButtonClick function isn't defined correctly. Check that you've added it inside your component with the proper TypeScript typing for button click events.

steps.title: Return a container div
steps.instruction: In the return statement of your EventTypingDemo component, replace the existing div with a div that has a className of 'container'.
steps.hint: Update the opening div tag to include className='container' while keeping the h1 element inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div element with className='container' containing the h1 heading.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div element
The h1 element remains inside the div
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a container div with the correct className. This provides a structural wrapper for your component's content.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added className='container' to the div element and kept the h1 inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container div with className='container' wasn't properly added. Check that you're returning a div with className='container' containing the h1 element.

steps.title: Add a text input field
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add an input element of type 'text' with value={text} and onChange={handleInputChange}.
steps.hint: Use the JSX <input> element with type='text'. Set its value to the text state variable and onChange to the handleInputChange function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A text input field appears in the UI, bound to the text state and the handleInputChange function.
successCriteria: The input element must have type='text', value={text}, and onChange={handleInputChange}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a text input field with proper TypeScript event typing. The input is now bound to the text state and will update it when the user types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input element, but it's missing one or more required attributes. Make sure it has type='text', value={text}, and onChange={handleInputChange}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or incorrect. Add an <input> element with type='text', value={text}, and onChange={handleInputChange} inside the container div.

steps.title: Add a checkbox input
steps.instruction: Add an input element of type 'checkbox' inside the container div, with checked={isChecked} and onChange={handleCheckboxChange}
steps.hint: Create an <input> element with type='checkbox', and connect it to your state and handler using the checked and onChange props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a checkbox input element that uses the isChecked state and handleCheckboxChange handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a checkbox input with proper TypeScript event typing. The checkbox is now connected to your state and handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a checkbox, but it's missing some required attributes. Make sure to include type='checkbox', checked={isChecked}, and onChange={handleCheckboxChange}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The checkbox input wasn't added correctly. Check that you're adding an <input> element with the correct type and props inside the container div.

steps.title: Add a button with click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the container div with onClick={handleButtonClick} and text content 'Click me'.
steps.hint: Use the <button> JSX element with the onClick prop set to the handleButtonClick function you defined earlier.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with typed click handler
<button onClick={handleButtonClick}>
  Click me
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now have a button that, when clicked, triggers the handleButtonClick function.
successCriteria: The button element must be present with onClick={handleButtonClick} and display 'Click me' as its text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button with proper TypeScript event typing. The button will call your handleButtonClick function when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it's missing either the onClick handler or the correct text content. Make sure to include onClick={handleButtonClick} and 'Click me' as the button text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or incorrectly implemented. Add a <button> element with onClick={handleButtonClick} and text content 'Click me'.

steps.title: Display current state values
steps.instruction: Add two paragraph elements inside the container div to display the current 'text' and 'isChecked' state values. Place them after the existing elements.
steps.hint:
Use JSX curly braces to embed the state variables in paragraph elements. For example:

Current text: {text}
steps.expectedOutcome: Two paragraph elements that show the current text and checkbox state values.
successCriteria:
The code should include two

elements that display the 'text' and 'isChecked' state variables using JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added paragraphs to display the current state values. This completes the Event Typing Demo component.
steps.feedbackPartial:
You've added some paragraphs, but make sure you have two separate

elements displaying both 'text' and 'isChecked' state values.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraphs displaying state values are missing or incorrect. Add two

elements that show the current 'text' and 'isChecked' values.
